# Test fixtures

`sample-with-author.png` — a minimal 1×1 RGB PNG with a tEXt chunk
carrying `Author=Linus Torvalds`. Used by `tests/full-flow.spec.js`.

## Source

Programmatically generated by `scripts/generate-test-fixture.mjs`
(no third-party content). The script is checked into this repo and
re-runnable from the project root:

```bash
node scripts/generate-test-fixture.mjs
```

The generator writes a fully-valid PNG byte-for-byte using only
Node's built-in `node:zlib` (deflate) and the standard PNG chunk
format. No external image library is involved.

## Why PNG and not JPG

Phase 8's privacy guard test and full-flow test both need a fixture
file. The brief originally mentioned "small JPG with known metadata
(GPS coordinates)". We deviated to a PNG-with-tEXt fixture because:

1. **The Writer path matters for full-flow.** The full-flow test clicks
   "Borrar todo" and needs the Done view to appear so it can verify
   the download button. An earlier session (Phase 9 discovery) found
   that ExifTool's vendored WASM runtime cannot round-trip a minimal
   1×1 JPEG: it can READ it but the WRITER returns an error.
   Switching the fixture to PNG avoids that runtime limitation.
2. **PNG tEXt chunks are well-supported.** ExifTool reads PNG tEXt
   chunks as `PNG:<keyword>` and emits them with a group prefix.
   MetaLimpia's parser strips the prefix and classifies `Author`
   into the `author` group, exactly as it would for a JPG's EXIF.
3. **Author is enough to assert the workflow.** The full-flow test
   only needs to see "metadata appears in groups" and "the cleanup
   completes" — the exact metadata name doesn't matter.

## Format / structure

| Property       | Value            |
|----------------|------------------|
| File size      | ~70 bytes        |
| Image          | 1×1, 8-bit RGB   |
| Color          | Red (#FF0000)    |
| Metadata       | `Author=Linus Torvalds` (tEXt chunk) |
